n: Spot it: The single bone above the eyes, running back to the coronal suture.
Don't confuse: Parietal bones sit behind the coronal suture.
Spot it: The big curved plates on top, between the coronal suture (front), sagittal suture (midline), lambdoid (back), and squamous (side).
Spot it: Lateral skull around the ear hole, with the mastoid behind and the zygomatic process reaching forward.
Spot it: Posterior skull below the lambdoid suture, wrapping under to the big hole.
Don't confuse: Parietal bones are above the lambdoid suture.
Spot it: Inside the cranial floor: the butterfly with the sella turcica in the middle.
Spot it: Cranial floor: the small sieve-like plate with a fin (crista galli) between the eye sockets. In the nose: conchae and the upper septum.
Spot it: The bone holding the upper teeth, from the teeth up to the side of the nose and the eye floor.
Spot it: The prominent cheek below and lateral to the eye.
Spot it: The thin pair at the top of the nasal opening, between the frontal processes of the maxillae.
Spot it: A tiny thin plate on the inside wall of the eye socket near the nose, with the tear-duct groove.
Spot it: Underside of the skull: the back third of the roof of the mouth, behind the maxilla's palatine processes.
Spot it: Front view: the lower half of the center plate in the nose. Back/underside view: the whole center plate.
Spot it: The U-shaped bone with the lower teeth and the vertical rami.
Don't confuse: The maxilla holds the upper teeth.
Spot it: A floating horseshoe under the jaw, above the Adam's apple.
Spot it: The ossicle with the long handle.
Don't confuse: Incus = anvil (middle). Stapes = stirrup (last).
Spot it: The tooth-shaped middle bone with two legs.
Don't confuse: Malleus = hammer. Stapes = stirrup.
Spot it: A tiny stirrup shape with an arch and a footplate.
Don't confuse: Malleus and incus come before it.
Spot it: Runs side to side across the top of the skull, like a headband.
Don't confuse: Sagittal runs front to back. Lambdoid is at the back.
Spot it: Runs front to back down the center of the top of the skull.
Don't confuse: The coronal suture crosses side to side.
Spot it: An upside-down V on the back of the skull.
Don't confuse: The coronal suture is at the front.
Spot it: An arched line on the side of the skull above the ear.
Don't confuse: The lambdoid suture is at the back. The coronal suture is at the front.
Spot it: Inside view, top-down: the front step, above the eye sockets.
Don't confuse: The middle fossa is the butterfly-shaped dip in the middle.
Spot it: The butterfly-shaped depression around the sella turcica.
Don't confuse: Anterior = front shelf. Posterior = big back bowl.
Spot it: The big bowl around the foramen magnum.
Don't confuse: The middle fossa is in front of the petrous ridges.
Spot it: A hollow in the forehead above the nose (sagittal cut or X-ray).
Don't confuse: The maxillary sinus is in the cheek.
Spot it: The flat midline spot between the brow ridges.
Don't confuse: The supraorbital margins are the rims over each eye.
Spot it: The curved bony brow edge over each orbit.
Don't confuse: The infraorbital margin is the lower rim.
Spot it: A small opening on the upper rim of the eye socket, toward the middle.

alts: Zygomatic process of the frontal bone
n: Spot it: The lateral corner of the orbit, above the frontozygomatic suture.
Spot it: Faint arcs on the side of the skull, above the squamous suture.
Spot it: The midline knob on the back of the skull. You can feel it on your own head.
Don't confuse: The nuchal lines run sideways from it.
Spot it: Horizontal ridges across the back of the occipital bone, beside the protuberance.
Spot it: The huge hole in the skull base.
Don't confuse: The jugular foramen and hypoglossal canals are much smaller and sit beside it.
Spot it: Two oval rocker bumps flanking the foramen magnum on the underside.
Spot it: A small tunnel just above the occipital condyles, on the side wall of the foramen magnum.

alts: Squamous portion of the temporal bone
n: Spot it: The flat fan above the ear on the side of the skull.

alts: Petrous portion of the temporal bone
n: Spot it: Inside the skull floor: the dense, angled ridge of the temporal bone that splits the middle fossa from the posterior fossa. It holds the inner ear.
Don't confuse: The squamous portion is the thin flat fan on the outside wall.
Spot it: Side view: the big hole above the mastoid and behind the mandibular fossa.
Spot it: Inside the skull: a hole on the back face of the petrous ridge.
Spot it: The rounded knob pointing down behind the ear canal.
Don't confuse: The styloid process is the thin needle in front of and medial to it.
Spot it: The pencil-like spike pointing down under the ear, in front of the mastoid.
Spot it: The tiny hole directly between the styloid and mastoid.
Don't confuse: The jugular foramen is more medial.

alts: Zygomatic process of the temporal bone
n: Spot it: The arch segment starting just in front of the ear.
Spot it: Underside: a round hole just in front of the jugular foramen, medial to the styloid. Inside: it opens near the foramen lacerum.
Spot it: An irregular opening beside the foramen magnum, behind the carotid canal.
Spot it: The midline saddle in the center of the cranial floor, between the middle fossae.
Don't confuse: The crista galli is the fin in front of it.

alts: Greater wing of the sphenoid bone
n: Spot it: The big curved plates that sweep out to each side from the sphenoid body. They form the floor of the middle fossa and show on the side of the skull in front of the temporal bone.
Don't confuse: The lesser wings are the thin, pointed shelves in front, at the back edge of the anterior fossa.

alts: Lesser wing of the sphenoid bone
n: Spot it: The thin, pointed shelves on top of the sphenoid, making the back edge of the anterior fossa. The optic canals pass through their base.
Don't confuse: The greater wings are the larger plates below and behind, in the middle fossa.
Spot it: Inside: round holes at the base of the lesser wings, just in front of the sella.
Spot it: At the back of the orbit: a slanted slit beside and below the optic canal.
Spot it: A horizontal slit low in the eye socket.
Don't confuse: The superior orbital fissure is the higher, diagonal slit behind the optic canal.
Spot it: The most anterior of the three, right under the superior orbital fissure.
Don't confuse: Ovale is larger and behind it.
Spot it: Inside view: the oval hole behind the foramen rotundum, in the middle fossa.
Don't confuse: Rotundum is round and more anterior.
Spot it: The tiny hole just behind and lateral to the foramen ovale.
Don't confuse: Ovale is bigger and just in front.
Spot it: A jagged hole at the tip of the petrous ridge, beside the sella.
Don't confuse: The foramen ovale is the neat oval just lateral to it.
Spot it: Underside, behind the last molars: the broader of the two vertical plates, the outer one.
Spot it: Underside: the thinner plate closer to the midline, beside the back of the nose.
Spot it: Inside view: the little midline spike between the two cribriform plates.

alts: Cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone
n: Spot it: Inside view: the sieve-like strips on both sides of the crista galli.

alts: Perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone
n: Spot it: Front view into the nose: the top half of the middle wall.
Spot it: Front view into the nose: the curled shelves on the side walls.
Spot it: A hole at the lower inner corner of the orbit.

alts: Horizontal plate of the palatine bone
n: Spot it: Underside: the back third of the roof of the mouth, behind the palatine processes of the maxillae.
Don't confuse: The palatine process of the maxilla is the front two-thirds.
Spot it: Underside: tiny holes at the back corners of the palate, by the last molars.
Spot it: The bony arch the upper teeth sit in.
Spot it: The tiny spike at the bottom center of the nose hole.
Don't confuse: The mental protuberance is on the chin, not this.
Spot it: The strip between the nasal bone and the orbit.
Spot it: A small hole on the face just below the eye socket rim.
Spot it: Underside: the front of the roof of the mouth, behind the teeth.
Spot it: The part of the maxilla below the cheek that joins the zygomatic bone.
Spot it: The curved bottom edge of the eye socket.
Don't confuse: The supraorbital margin is the top edge.

alts: Temporal process of the zygomatic bone
n: Spot it: The front half of the cheek arch.
Spot it: The whole bar running from cheek to ear. Feel it in front of your ear.
Don't confuse: Only the halves have process names.
Spot it: The horizontal U from chin to angle.
Don't confuse: The ramus is vertical.
Spot it: The upright plate behind the teeth, rising toward the ear.
Spot it: The back lower corner of the jaw, below the ear.
Spot it: The bony ridge the lower teeth sit in.
Spot it: The vertical line at the center of the chin.
Don't confuse: The mental foramina are the holes to each side.
Spot it: The holes on the outer jaw below the premolars, one on each side.
Spot it: The inside face of the ramus, mid-height.
Don't confuse: The mental foramen is on the outside front of the body.
Spot it: The front, pointed post at the top of the ramus. A chewing muscle (temporalis) attaches here.
Don't confuse: The condylar process is the back post with the rounded head.
Spot it: The back post at the top of the ramus, ending in the rounded head that meets the temporal bone at the jaw joint.
Don't confuse: The coronoid process is the front, pointed post.
Spot it: The oval head right in front of the ear canal, sitting in the mandibular fossa.
Spot it: The scoop at the top of the ramus, between the two posts.
Don't confuse: Don't name the posts; the question wants the dip.
